tags.PROPOSED: Claude's mechanism, not yet ruled on
tags.untagged: PROPOSED unless it quotes the owner or v11

signals.name: smile
signals.meaning: a desire was satisfied (meaning PROPOSED; the owner defined cry, crying, screaming)

signals.name: crying
signals.meaning: you gave me something, it was not what I desired

signals.name: screaming
signals.meaning: you gave me something else, still not what I desired

rules: idea rule: values of an observed equation become variables (BUILT v9)
constructor principle: a claim holds if it holds at the base and survives every constructor (BUILT v10)
observe: the change-set of cells each turn is the student's input (DESIGN)
obligation: the smallest open desire becomes the next signal or question (BUILT, re-scoped)

heads.note: whether V12 is born with these or must earn them is undecided

levels.name: point
levels.can_emit: the id of a cell or neuron it wants attention on
levels.unlock: first change-set it observes that contains a cell it wrote itself (first 'me do')

levels.name: echo
levels.can_emit: an expression it holds, verbatim (a stored term)
levels.unlock: it applies a teacher's row itself and the resulting change matches the teacher's earlier demonstration

levels.name: answer
levels.can_emit: a computed value with its receipt
levels.unlock: it proves its first law by induction, unaided

levels.name: explain
levels.can_emit: a why: the cause chain behind a change
levels.unlock: it answers a teacher's 'why did you gain neurons' with a complete receipt, unaided

levels.name: speak
levels.can_emit: sentences: cons chains of words as gates
levels.unlock: a word gate acquires a DNA path to a numeric gate (the word cluster joins 0), unaided

receipt.form: n<neuron#>·i<gate#>·s<shard#>·o<gate#> repeated; ends when o == i
receipt.rule: neuron numbers, gate numbers and shard numbers are each one global counter; the gate's expression is its graph location

stages.name: birth
stages.student: one neuron, six blank sheets, four signals; emits cry at end of turn (PROPOSED: an open desire, nothing to satisfy it)
expect: neuron count 1
all sheets empty
voice level 0
structure signature recorded

stages.name: constructors
stages.teacher: writes op S/1 on 0 to hearing with APPLY=install, in front of the student; then op P/1 on 0; v11 declared P at turn 12
stages.student: observes hearing row, then sight/touch rows change; emits smile when its open desire (something to observe) is met
expect: S and P states born
sight rows show BORN > 0 with WHO=structure, caused by a teacher row
student's first cell write attempt may be garbage; the structure records it with WHO=student; the teacher writes RIGHT/WRONG=wrong
voice level 1 when the change-set contains a cell the student wrote

stages.name: addition
stages.teacher: writes x+0 -> x, x+S(y) -> S(x+y), S(P(x)) -> x, P(S(x)) -> x, x+P(y) -> P(x+y); asks 1+1?, 2+3?; asks who/what/why of each change; asks 'can you apply the next one yourself'
stages.student: answers by applying rows itself (APPLY with WHO=student); proves S/P lemmas, left zero, commutativity from its own cases
expect: 2 lemmas proved unaided in this range (v11 turn 15); left zero and commutativity followed at v11 turn 20
voice level 1 then 2
at least one wrong self-installed belief, corrected by the teacher and recorded as an episode

stages.name: negation and subtraction
stages.teacher: writes neg(0), neg(S(x)), neg(P(x)), x - y -> x + neg(y); asks 3 - 5?; asks why the answer is negative
stages.student: applies, computes 3-5 = P(P(0)), answers why with a receipt
expect: subtraction answers with receipts
voice level 3 on first unaided proof in this stage

stages.name: multiplication and powers
stages.teacher: writes x*0, x*S(y), x*P(y), x^0, x^S(y); asks 7*8?, 2^10?; then asks 'why did you gain neurons' (968 births measured in v11; the question was not asked in v11)
stages.student: computes 2^10 by unary; answers the why from its receipt (the answer text is OPEN — not scripted)
expect: 2^10 = 1024 with ~968 births (measured in v11)
voice level 4 when the why is answered from the receipt
the internal sheet's CAUSE for the births is filled by the student, not by the structure

stages.name: positional notation
stages.teacher: writes digit constructors and carry laws with revisit; asks 100*100?; asks 'which route did you take and why'
stages.student: recomputes known unary arrivals through the cheaper route; unary routes stay in DNA as provenance
expect: 100*100 answers without the depth brake
why 100*100 shows the positional route; unary route for 2^10 still recoverable from DNA
no neuron deleted

stages.name: division, gcd, fractions
stages.teacher: writes three-way compare, long division by repeated subtraction, Euclid gcd, lowest terms (v7 laws)
stages.student: applies; proposes and proves at least one law about division unaided
expect: 10100/2, gcd, lowest terms answer
one unaided proof in this stage
a wrong belief about division is installed, contradicted, retracted, and recorded

stages.name: order, logic, conditionals
stages.teacher: writes lt/eq/gt over numbers, and/or/not over true/false, if(c, a, b); asks is 3 < 5?, is (3<5) and (2<1)?
stages.student: computes truth values; proves de Morgan or a similar law from cases
expect: boolean laws proved unaided
if reduces only when its condition settles

stages.name: counting, sets, ratio
stages.teacher: writes lists (cons/nil) of numbers, length, member, count-if, and ratio as a pair (num, den) in lowest terms; asks 'of these six outcomes how many are even' and 'what fraction'
stages.student: computes counts and ratios; the pair (favorable, total) is the first probability
expect: ratio answers in lowest terms
student names the pair as a fraction using its own word once taught

stages.name: probability and statistics
stages.teacher: writes sum, mean as sum/length, frequency table, and probability of an event as count-if/length; asks about coin and die lists; asks 'what do you expect' then shows the outcome
stages.student: computes means and probabilities; records EXPECTED vs outcome on the internal sheet; a refuted expectation becomes a why
expect: mean and P(event) over given lists
EXPECTED column populated by the student
a refuted expectation asked about unaided

stages.name: words as gates
stages.teacher: writes sentences and facts (isa) as in v11; then asks the student to relate a word to a number it already holds (three apples, three forks)
stages.student: connects a word gate to a numeric gate by a DNA row it writes itself; voice level 5
expect: the word cluster reaches 0 by at least one DNA path
voice level 5: the student emits a sentence
the 'three of a kind' idea appears as a hypothesis from co-arrival
